questions.question: Which description fits the **Coverage** resource?
options: Financial instrument which may be used to reimburse or pay for health care products and services.
This resource provides enrollment and plan details from the processing of an EnrollmentRequest resource.

This resource provides patient and insurance coverage information to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an CoverageEligibilityResponse, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is…
This resource provides the insurance enrollment details to the insurer regarding a specified coverage.
questions.explanation: **Coverage**: Financial instrument which may be used to reimburse or pay for health care products and services. Includes both insurance and self-payment. The other descriptions belong to **EnrollmentResponse**, **CoverageEligibilityRequest**, **EnrollmentRequest**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? Record the patient’s health insurance policy and member number.
questions.explanation: **Coverage**. Who pays: the insurance cover itself.

questions.question: You know **Coverage**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “the product offered by an insurer”?
questions.explanation: **InsurancePlan**: the product offered by an insurer. **Coverage** is for something else: Financial instrument which may be used to reimburse or pay for health care products and services.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **Coverage** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of Coverage are `status` (1..1), `beneficiary` (1..1), `payor` (1..*). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **Coverage** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of Coverage: `status`. `status`: active | cancelled | draft | entered-in-error. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
